10.1007_s00604-026-07874-2: An electrochemical chiral sensor based on β-cyclodextrin@Ti3C2Tx MXene/screen printed carbon electrode (β-CD@MXene/SPCE) was developed for the determination of D- and L-tyrosine enantiomers for the first time. Morphological characterization of the material (β-CD@MXene) was performed using Field Emission-Scanning Electron Microscopy (FE-SEM) and Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) imaging, while X-ray Diffraction (XRD) and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) confirmed the crystalline structure and interaction between MXene and β-CD in structural characterization. To evaluate the electrochemical characterization of the modified electrodes, cyclic voltammetry (CV) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) techniques were applied. To investigate the electrochemical behavior of the tested D- and L-amino acid enantiomers, CV and differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) techniques were conducted. Among the tested chiral species, only D- and L-tyrosine showed distinct voltammetric signals. To investigate the electrochemical behavior of D- and L-tyrosine, CV and DPV techniques were conducted revealing an increase in oxidation peak currents with the increasing tyrosine concentration levels. The voltammetric response of racemic D/L-tyrosine was also examined. For real sample analysis, human serum was used in chronoamperometric measurements (10–100 µM), yielding a linear response. The LOD and LOQ values were 3.15 µM and 9.45 µM, respectively, for D-tyrosine, and 4.68 µM and 14.05 µM, respectively, for L-tyrosine in human serum samples.
10.1016_j.est.2026.122872: Accurately estimating the state of health of a battery is essential for the safe and efficient operation of electric vehicles. However, performing this estimation under real-world conditions poses significant challenges, as only limited measurement data - current, voltage, and temperature - are available during vehicle operation. This work presents a data-driven framework for state of health estimation based on automatic feature extraction. To reveal battery degradation patterns, incremental capacity curves derived from constant charge phases are analyzed. Through proper orthogonal decomposition, the dimensionality of the feature space is reduced while preserving essential information. These extracted features are then used to train a machine learning model for accurate state of health estimation. The framework can process partial charge segments from different state of charge regions, overcoming the limitation of requiring complete charge cycles. This capability makes the method particularly suitable for onboard implementation in electric vehicles. Validation is performed using data from large-scale aging experiments that include both structured test cycles and dynamic charging conditions. The model consistently captures degradation trends, confirming its robustness and suitability for use in onboard state of health monitoring of electric vehicles.
10.1016_j.ijhydene.2026.156509: Photoelectrochemical water splitting offers a sustainable route for solar hydrogen production, with hematite (α-Fe 2 O 3 ) attractive due to its abundance, stability, and suitable band gap. However, achieving high-performance, uniform, and optically tunable photoanodes is limited by the nonlinear interplay between film architecture, porosity, and interfacial charge-transfer processes. Here, we present a data-driven nonlinear design strategy using Design of Experiments and response surface methodology to optimize hematite photoelectrodes fabricated via an integrated physical–electrochemical route on FTO substrates. Key fabrication parameters were systematically tuned to balance photon absorption, charge transport, and surface kinetics. This multivariate approach reduced experimental runs by ∼60% and energy consumption by ∼50%, identifying optimal conditions for functional synergy. The optimized bare hematite delivers 1.5 mA cm −2 at 1.6 V vs. RHE and exhibits excellent long-term photoelectrochemical stability, among the highest reported for physically deposited non-modified hematite, driven by improved donor density, crystallinity, and reduced charge-transfer resistance.
10.1021_jacs.6c05085: We report an electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction catalyzed by a paramagnetic and conductive CuO/Cu interface with spins polarized by a moderate external magnetic field (MF) of ∼800 gauss, achieving a ∼30% increase in CO2-to-C2+ Faradaic efficiency (FE) compared to that in the absence of the MF in a flow cell electrolyzer. At a current density of 400 mA/cm2, the CO2-to-C2+ FE reached 86.7 ± 2.7% with 47.9 ± 1.4% cathodic energy efficiency (EE) in contrast to the CO2-to-C2+ FE of 67.6% with 36.4% of EE in the absence of MF. Notably, ethanol production exhibits a much higher response to the MF (∼55.6% increase in FE) than ethylene (∼6.4% increase in FE) at 400 mA/cm2. In situ surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) captured magnetic-field-enhanced *CO coverage and ethanol-forming C2 intermediates on CuO/Cu, providing direct spectroscopic evidence of spin-modulated pathway selection. Computational study suggests that the enhancement of ethanol selectivity is due to the reduced reaction kinetic barrier under MF, while the ethylene selectivity is less affected, mainly due to the insensitivity of the kinetic barriers under MF.
